clue.text: Corner portion turned over

indicators.note: turned over tells us the word for portion is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a portion is a part

explanation.surface: A slice of something in a corner has been flipped upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to trap them, leaving no escape route.

clue.text: Grass receives money for detecting

indicators.note: receives means one piece takes the other into its middle

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone, as is to sing
a cent is a small coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: An informer is paid off for spotting wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like lawn but is the verb for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenting is picking up a smell, so a synonym for detecting something by nose.

clue.text: No Greek character is socially unacceptable

parts.note: taken as written
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Claiming that no Greek letter is socially acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and not-upper-class British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U is a dated British label for manners or words not used by the upper class, hence socially unacceptable.

clue.text: A CD initially available in the library

definitions.text: A CD initially available in the library

parts.words: A CD initially available in the library
parts.note: CD are the initials of Charles Dickens, so this is one of his novels on the library shelf, not a compact disc

explanation.surface: A compact disc can first be borrowed from the library.
explanation.walkthrough: CD looks like a music disc; read as initials it is the author, Charles Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dickens novel is a book by the writer whose initials are C.D., available to borrow.

clue.text: Birdies? Not one! Playing rubbish!

indicators.note: playing suggests the remaining letters are put into play in a new order
not tells us a piece is left out of the word before it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A golfer's lament: not a single birdie, and the play is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' removes an I from BIRDIES, leaving BIRDES, which 'Playing' rearranges. A birdie is one under par on a golf hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or wreckage left lying around.

clue.text: Old issue to support value of arithmetic

parts.note: to back something is to support it
a number is a value used in arithmetic

explanation.surface: An old problem resurfaces to bolster the importance of maths.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is a past issue of a magazine or newspaper, so an old issue.

clue.text: Good man to fit in firm

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a crossword convention for a good man
fit as in capable, able

explanation.surface: A good man is taken on to suit a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and firm, not wobbling.

clue.text: Non-striker backs up, but striker's fifth out

indicators.note: out means that letter is removed
in a down entry, up means the word backs is written bottom to top
fifth picks the fifth letter of the word striker's

explanation.surface: A batsman at the non-striker's end backs up, but the striker is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BACKS into SKCAB; 'out' removes K, the fifth letter of striker. The cricket surface misleads: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a worker who refuses to strike, literally a non-striker.

clue.text: One page of the directory

indicators.note: of suggests the answer is a part taken from inside the following word

explanation.surface: A single page from the telephone book.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the right-hand page of an open book, one of the two pages.

clue.text: Intolerant etc in sail at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A seemingly random list of words about intolerance while sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means unable to stretch or give, hence intolerant of change.

clue.text: Office worker able to scratch a living?

definitions.meaning: read literally: someone who earns a crust by scratching a nib across paper

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an office worker can just about make ends meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a dismissive term for a clerk doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Piecemeal?

parts.note: read as a meal made of pieces: chunks of meat on a skewer

explanation.surface: A single word asking whether something is done bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is food in pieces threaded on a skewer, literally a piece meal.

clue.text: City fashion

parts.note: the phrase shipshape and ... fashion names a West of England port city and means neat and in order

explanation.surface: Clothing trends seen in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol is a port city in south-west England; 'shipshape and Bristol fashion' means tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a city, and the phrase Bristol fashion means in good order.

clue.text: Graduate gets line on South American tree

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
SA stands for South America

explanation.surface: A graduate writes a line about a tree from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree with very light wood.

clue.text: Trace rat to broken earthenware

indicators.note: broken signals that these letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Following a rat's trail to some broken pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed brownish-red earthenware, used for pots.

clue.text: Most sharp, but with greatest confidence about nothing!

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: surest means most certain, with greatest confidence
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Sounding very sharp while being supremely confident about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour means sharp to the taste, so most sour is most sharp.

clue.text: Painter, one to be uplifted — a great man!

indicators.note: uplifted here means lifted out and removed

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An artist tipped to be raised up as a great figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifted' sounds like praise but means the I is lifted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of great stature or power, from the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Drink period between opposite sides

indicators.note: between puts one piece in the middle of the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, opposite sides
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Having a drink in the interval between two opposing teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a type of drink.

clue.text: Money coming from various directions

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
E is east, a compass direction
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Cash flowing in from all sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The sen is a small unit of currency in Japan and elsewhere in Asia.

clue.text: See 4
7 unfinished, collapsing in an explosion

indicators.note: collapsing suggests the letters fall into a new order
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: refers to the answer at 7 down

explanation.surface: A firm, incomplete and falling down, ends in a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7-down answer loses its last letter E, and 'collapsing' rearranges STABL.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a sudden explosion or its shock wave.

clue.text: Lady holds new account concerning a boa

indicators.note: holds means one piece contains the others

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
on means concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A woman keeps a fresh record about a snake, or a feather scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a boa' looks like a stole; it is the snake family.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a large South American snake of the boa family.

clue.text: Structure federal agency to make a comeback, although antiquated

parts.note: an arch is a curved structure

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so this word is turned round

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A building scheme for a government agency's return, despite being dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means very old or old-fashioned, the same as antiquated.

clue.text: Bow down to play the bells in church

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring is to sound bells

explanation.surface: Kneeling to sound the bells during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to shrink or cower, bowing down in fear.

clue.text: Cabot left to travel the blue

indicators.note: to travel suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: The explorer Cabot sets out on the blue ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cabot was a 15th-century explorer who sailed from Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a deep blue colour, from the metal used in blue pigment.

clue.text: Hanging of murderer takes place without universal right

indicators.note: taking a place outside means the first piece sits around the others

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: A murderer's execution is held without any general right.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a hanging, a piece of fabric hung at a window.

clue.text: Animal with one horn? Possibly

parts.note: one horn suggests the mythical unicorn, but some real thick-skinned beasts have a single horn, others two, hence possibly

explanation.surface: Asking whether a beast has a single horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Some species of rhinoceros, like the Indian one, have a single horn.

clue.text: Degree row

definitions.meaning: a level or grade, as in military standing
a line of people or things

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means both a degree of status and a row or line.

clue.text: Aggressive libels come out, millions being lost

indicators.note: out signals the letters come out in another arrangement
being lost means a piece is taken away

explanation.surface: Fierce defamations come to light, costing millions.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from LIBELS COME, and 'out' rearranges LIBELSCOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means warlike and eager to fight, hence aggressive.

clue.text: Disdainful, not first or second, uncertain

indicators.note: the opening two letters are dropped

parts.note: sniffy means scornful, disdainful

explanation.surface: Scornful, but not first or second, and unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or uncertain.

clue.text: Large vessel with sheep on the river

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A big boat carrying sheep down the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Sir, we hear, has staff for late entertainment

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
a club is a heavy stick or staff

explanation.surface: A titled man carries a walking stick for an evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue offering entertainment late at night.

clue.text: Sweet stall

definitions.meaning: a soft confection made of sugar, butter and milk
to evade or play for time, avoiding a straight answer

explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is both a soft sweet and a verb meaning to dodge or stall.
